        <script>
        function dayCount(targetISO){
          const now = new Date();
          const target = new Date(targetISO);
          const ms = target - now;
          if (ms < 0) return "DONE";
          const d = Math.ceil(ms / (1000*60*60*24));
          return d + (d===1 ? " day" : " days");
        }
        document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
          document.querySelectorAll("[data-final]").forEach(el => {
            el.textContent = dayCount(el.getAttribute("data-final"));
          });
        });
        </script>

## How to use this site

1. **Read the per-course Overview pages first.** They each open with the strategy that drives every other page.
2. **Memorize before you practice.** Each course has a one-page Cram Sheet. Get it cold *before* opening any mock exam.
3. **Practice deliberately, not passively.** Active Recall Banks force retrieval. Mock exams simulate pressure. Killer Traps target the predictable mistakes.
4. **For IR 362 specifically:** the four research deep-dives are the moat. Read them, then map each onto Hammad's 17 study-guide questions using the Framework.
5. **Use the search bar (top right)** to jump to any concept by name.

## Course strategy at a glance

::: {.panel-tabset}

### IR 362 — heaviest weight, essay format

**Strategy:** Build *six* essay-bank thesis statements you can deploy across any of Hammad's 17 study-guide questions. The questions are not independent — they revolve around the **API → Abraham Accords pivot**, the **Nash equilibrium "carousel,"** and **Iran's linkage role** between the two regional spheres. Master those three throughlines and the 17 questions become recombinations of the same material.

- Framework with all 17 questions: [ir362/index.qmd](ir362/index.qmd)
- Iran's regional engine: [ir362/iran-axis.qmd](ir362/iran-axis.qmd)
- Abraham Accords + Saudi normalization: [ir362/abraham-accords.qmd](ir362/abraham-accords.qmd)
- Nash equilibrium + the carousel: [ir362/nash-equilibrium.qmd](ir362/nash-equilibrium.qmd)
- Syria — Iran alliance and the December 2024 collapse: [ir362/syria-collapse.qmd](ir362/syria-collapse.qmd)
- One-page cram sheet: [ir362/cram-sheet.qmd](ir362/cram-sheet.qmd)

::: {.callout-warning}
**Source-coverage gaps in the local research library** — these are flagged in the Framework and the deep-dives:

- **Q10 (Nash equilibrium)**: Hammad assigned a specific article + slide. **Check Brightspace.** The deep-dive scaffolds the canonical IR-game-theory canon (Schelling, Fearon, Jervis, Axelrod) but cannot substitute for the assigned reading.
- **Q16 (Iran/Hezbollah/Syria)**: deep-dive triangulates Nasr / Parsi / Goodarzi / Norton — confirm against the syllabus.
- **Q6 + Q13/Q14 (Syrian collapse + carousel)**: lecture-based; carousel is Hammad's own framing.
:::

### ECON 205 — Mon May 11, 2:00–4:00 PM

**Strategy:** Cumulative final, ~70% post-midterm material. Pencil + calculator only. The exam tests *application* — given a scenario, can you pick the right model and execute the algebra. Cram-sheet memorization happens *before* exam day, not on it.

5-day plan (Wed May 6 → Mon May 11):

| Day | Focus | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| Wed 5/6 | Read Cram Sheet · run Active Recall Bank §1 (pre-midterm) | 30 cards correct in a row |
| Thu 5/7 | Active Recall §2 (Money/Inflation, Fluctuations, Fiscal) | Mock Exam A diagnostic |
| Fri 5/8 | Mock Exam A under timed conditions · review key | Identify 5 weak spots |
| Sat 5/9 | Killer Traps · drill the 5 weak spots | Trap-drill score ≥ 80% |
| Sun 5/10 | Mock Exam B under timed conditions · review key | Net error rate ≤ 10% |
| Mon 5/11 | Light skim of Cram Sheet · 90 min walk · sleep · exam | — |

Start here: [econ205/index.qmd](econ205/index.qmd)

### ACCT 410x — date TBD

**Strategy:** Leventhal "user-oriented" — emphasize *what the number means for a manager*, not journal-entry mechanics. The April 20 tutoring brief identified four high-yield trap areas (indirect cash flow, multi-product CVP, inventory error reversal, bond pricing). Drill those first.

Start here: [acct410x/index.qmd](acct410x/index.qmd)

:::

## Source-of-truth files

All this content is generated from markdown files in the same folder structure. To edit, open the source `.qmd` file in your editor and re-render (`quarto render`). The site is also pushed to GitHub Pages — see the repo for version history.

::: {.callout-tip}
**This site renders cleanly on phones.** Open it on Hanna's iPhone, bookmark it to her home screen, and study from anywhere.
:::
